question.text: Which of the following correctly describes DALYs averted as a social-impact metric?

answer.text: Disability-Adjusted Life Years averted — a non-monetary health impact metric combining mortality and morbidity reductions
Discounted Annual Lifetime Yields — a monetary return metric
Direct Annual Livelihood Yield — a livelihood metric
Daily Active Loan Users — a microfinance metric

explanation.text: The Logic: DALYs averted stands for Disability-Adjusted Life Years averted. It is a non-monetary health-impact metric that combines years of life lost due to premature mortality with years lived with disability (morbidity), producing a single composite figure. It is the standard WHO health-impact metric and is widely used in burden-of-disease studies. The Trap: The acronym DALY is specific to health economics. Options B, C and D invent plausible-sounding expansions ('Discounted Annual Lifetime Yields', 'Direct Annual Livelihood Yield', 'Daily Active Loan Users') that do not exist as standard metrics. Note: The DALY / Disability-Adjusted Life Years / DALYs-averted definition is not described in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) at pages 114, 159-160, 173, 177-180 or 190. The workbook lists other health indicators such as mortality, maternal deaths, institutional deliveries, screenings and immunisation. The framing above reflects general WHO / public-health-economics knowledge.
